- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent 7-day mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast mean.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — if true outcome deviates >3% from 14d moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- When official events are frequent (≥20/30d) and supply net is negative, model underestimates volatility — increase forecast standard deviation by 0.1–0.3x baseline.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum — apply exponential smoothing with decay factor 0.85 to sentiment-weighted average.
